progress: No change, in drafting at both ends while two coordinating bodies were created above it
summary: The [national digital transformation strategy](2026-02-16 Mozambique Launches Drafting of National Digital Transformation Strategy) is still unpublished, while an [agency](2026-03-16-sets-up-agency-digital-transformation-biometricupdate) and a [technical commission](2026-03-27-builds-institutional-framework-digital-transformation-wearetech) were created in March 2026.
developments:
Drafting was formally launched in February 2026, with more than 700 stakeholders engaged across six regional consultations and validation workshops, and no text published by August ([launch](2026-02-16 Mozambique Launches Drafting of National Digital Transformation Strategy), [engagement](2026-08-08-itu-vamoz-digital-project-mozambique)). A donor project recorded in January 2026 that its own strategy work had been deprioritised against the ministry's stated preference for implementation over new policy documents ([deprioritisation](2026-01-16-worldbank-mozambique-digital-acceleration-project-second-restructuring-paper)).

A Digital Transformation and Innovation Agency was created with a remit covering interoperability of state platforms, data-centre integration and procurement ([agency](2026-03-16-sets-up-agency-digital-transformation-biometricupdate)), and a Multisectoral Technical Commission by decree of 10 March 2026 ([commission](2026-03-27-builds-institutional-framework-digital-transformation-wearetech)). The integration roadmap the commission was to draft by mid-2026 is not on record.

summary: A [National Data Governance Policy, Strategy and Action Plan](2025-11-01-mozambique-zero-draft-2-national-data-governance-policy) was validated in December 2025 as a draft resolution and had not been adopted by July 2026.
developments:
Zero Draft 2 is written as a Council of Ministers resolution with its number and approval date left blank ([draft](2025-11-01-mozambique-zero-draft-2-national-data-governance-policy)).

It proposes an independent National Data Governance Council of eleven to seventeen members with expert seats appointed by presidential decree subject to a two-thirds confirmation vote of the assembly, sitting alongside a data protection authority the law has not yet created, with four data classification tiers and a jurisdiction claim over data affecting Mozambican citizens and entities wherever located ([workshop](2025-12-05-prioritizes-data-governance-digital-sovereignty-techafricanews), [diagnostic](2025-12-09-world-bank-data-governance-mozambique-final)).

Before it, government entities followed their own data policies with oversight implied across four institutions and coordination gaps between them ([inception](2025-06-19-uneca-intic-mozambique-data-governance-project-inception-report)).

summary: A [five-year domestic data-centre plan](2025-12-04-build-local-data-centres-cloud-regulations-techafricanews) was announced for bank and institutional hosting, and [licence categories](2026-06-08-issues-first-licenses-digital-operators-techafricanews) are to be extended to data centres and cloud platforms.
developments:
The communications minister announced in December 2025 a five-year plan to build domestic data centres hosting cloud services for banks and institutions, with an updated regulatory framework replacing current restrictions; no site, cost, operator or milestone is stated and no implementation document has followed ([plan](2025-12-04-build-local-data-centres-cloud-regulations-techafricanews)).

Extension of the digital-operator licence categories to data centres and cloud platforms was announced at the first licensing ceremony, with no date, draft or instrument ([extension](2026-06-08-issues-first-licenses-digital-operators-techafricanews)).

One provider states it will open two availability zones and that it is the first licensed in the advanced category, on its own account alone ([provider](2026-07-23-bubble-data-centers-moz)).

summary: [Data centre and cloud regulations](2026-02-18-approval-data-center-regulation) were approved by decree at the end of 2025, above a [2003 central-bank notice](2025-06-19-uneca-intic-mozambique-data-governance-project-inception-report) already requiring data centres to sit in the country.
developments:
The regulations were approved by Decrees 71/2025 and 72/2025, both of 31 December 2025, subject to a ninety-day vacatio legis, and carry provisions on data centres located abroad and on storage of information classified as state secret ([decrees](2026-02-18-approval-data-center-regulation)).

Operators running on the date of entry into force have one year to comply, and a data-centre operator licence waives the requirement for a separate cloud-computing licence ([decrees](2026-02-18-approval-data-center-regulation)).

The decree texts themselves are not held. The consultation drafts required registration of any data-centre operator whether or not the facility is in Mozambique, a resident legal representative for foreign providers, four resilience categories, financial-sector data confined to the two highest and classified information confined to private clouds on national territory ([drafts](2025-03-21-regulation-data-centres-cloud-includes-sanctions-clubofmozambique)); whether those provisions survived into the decrees is not established.

summary: [Internet Para Todos](2026-07-23-mozambique-portail-national-haut-debit) targets 80 per cent mobile penetration and 95 per cent territory coverage by 2030, and the President [pledged 5G in all districts](2026-06-22-chapo-pledges-5g-district-capitals-2027-clubofmozambique) by then.
developments:
The programme launched in March 2025 with the regulator stating targets of 80 per cent mobile penetration, 95 per cent territory coverage and 99 per cent network availability by 2030 ([programme](2026-07-23-mozambique-portail-national-haut-debit)); two held accounts state those targets differently ([programme](2026-07-23-mozambique-portail-national-haut-debit), [account](2025-07-16 Mozambique Digital Transformation Strategy (Market Intelligence))).

The President pledged 5G in provincial capitals, special economic zones and main tourist destinations by 2027 and in all districts and administrative posts by 2030 ([pledge](2026-06-22-chapo-pledges-5g-district-capitals-2027-clubofmozambique), [coverage](2026-06-22-5g-rollout-southern-africa-digital-hub-techafricanews)). No costing, financing plan or interim milestone is published for either.

summary: The [National Artificial Intelligence Strategy](2026-04-01-mozambique-enia-draft1-national-ai-strategy) is in final drafting on five principles and eight sectoral pillars, and was [presented to the national association](2026-08-25-intic-amia-mozambique-ai-strategy) in August 2026.
developments:
Draft 1 is held: five founding principles including data sovereignty, and eight sectoral pillars structured into short, medium and long-term objectives ([draft](2026-04-01-mozambique-enia-draft1-national-ai-strategy)).

Public consultations and provincial workshops are under way and the artificial-intelligence commission is to review before submission to the Council of Ministers; the institute consulted the largest mobile operator at its Maputo premises on 12 August 2026 ([consultation](2026-08-18-mozambique-national-ai-strategy-vodacom-techafricanews), [operator](2026-08-17-mozambique-intic-vodacom-ai-strategy-consultation)).

The draft was presented to the national artificial intelligence association later in August, described as still under development through open multi-sector consultation; no adoption date, budget or governance instrument is stated ([presentation](2026-08-25-intic-amia-mozambique-ai-strategy)).

summary: A [Cyber Security Law](2026-07-01-mocambique-lei-13-2026-seguranca-cibernetica-lei-14-2026-crimes-ciberneticos) and a [Cybercrime Law](2026-07-06-intic-mocambique-publica-leis-seguranca-cibernetica-crimes-ciberneticos) were published on 1 July 2026 and come into force on 29 September, with [regulations](2026-07-06-intic-mocambique-publica-leis-seguranca-cibernetica-crimes-ciberneticos) due within 180 days.
developments:
The Cyber Security Law was approved by the assembly in April 2026, promulgated in June and published on 1 July, creating a national incident response team seated in the ICT institute and, at articles 67 to 71, a Cyber Security Fund financed by a flat 1 per cent of licensed providers' prior-year gross revenue ([law](2026-07-01-mocambique-lei-13-2026-seguranca-cibernetica-lei-14-2026-crimes-ciberneticos), [approval](2026-04-17 Mozambique parliament unanimously approves Cyber Security Law)).

The Cybercrime Law was published alongside it, providing for preservation and collection of digital evidence and for international cooperation, and repealing six penal-code articles in favour of its own offences ([cybercrime law](2026-07-06-intic-mocambique-publica-leis-seguranca-cibernetica-crimes-ciberneticos)).

Neither set of implementing regulations had been made by August 2026, and the Cyber Security Fund's own operating rules are among what they are left to settle ([regulations](2026-07-06-intic-mocambique-publica-leis-seguranca-cibernetica-crimes-ciberneticos)).

summary: The [personal data protection bill](2026-08-26-clubofmozambique-intic-data-protection-legislation-oversight) was being prepared for submission to parliament in August 2026, with no text, timetable or tabling date published.
developments:
The agency's president stated in August 2026 that the draft is being prepared for submission; the Cabinet submission planned for June 2026 is not on record ([statement](2026-08-26-clubofmozambique-intic-data-protection-legislation-oversight)).

An independent review of the proposed law was published in September 2025 ([review](2025-09-23 Review of Mozambique's Proposed Personal Data Protection Law)), and the government was recorded as preparing it in July 2026 ([preparation](2026-07-23-mozambique-government-preparing-personal-data-protection-law)).

Until it passes, the country's data rules are scattered across a constitutional article, the electronic transactions law, banking and labour statutes and a 2003 central-bank notice, with a ratified regional convention and no domestic statute giving effect to it.

summary: The [electronic transactions licensing regime](2026-06-08-issues-first-licenses-digital-operators-techafricanews) issued its [first 19 licences](2026-06-08-issues-first-licenses-digital-operators-techafricanews) in June 2026, against about 170 companies under evaluation.
developments:
Nineteen licences were issued to digital operators in June 2026 of about 170 registered companies under evaluation ([licences](2026-06-08-issues-first-licenses-digital-operators-techafricanews)).

The fee is one national minimum wage plus 1 per cent of revenue annually from the next fiscal year ([regime](2026-06-08-issues-first-licenses-digital-operators-techafricanews), [diagnostic](2025-12-09-world-bank-data-governance-mozambique-final)). The regime had been in force with no licences issued a year earlier, so the movement here is the door opening rather than the rule changing.

summary: There is [no dedicated artificial-intelligence legislation](2026-08-17-mozambique-intic-copyright-ai-legislation); an [online copyright act](2026-08-17-mozambique-intic-copyright-ai-legislation) is in drafting and an [intellectual property strategy](2026-07-22-mozambique-pepi-ip-strategy-ai-patentability) mandates a patentability study.
developments:
The ICT institute's board chairman stated in August 2026 that the country still lacks dedicated artificial-intelligence legislation ([absence](2026-08-17-mozambique-intic-copyright-ai-legislation)).

An Online Copyright Protection Act is in drafting for introduction next year, its chairman naming authorship of artificial-intelligence output and liability for artificial-intelligence training as open questions the country has no law on; no draft text or introduction date is held ([drafting](2026-08-17-mozambique-intic-copyright-ai-legislation)).

An intellectual property policy and strategy to 2035, approved by resolution in June 2026, mandates a study of the patentability of inventions made by artificial intelligence and of the inventive-step and disclosure standards that should apply ([strategy](2026-07-22-mozambique-pepi-ip-strategy-ai-patentability), [account](2026-08-04-mozambique-to-examine-ai-patentability-under-new-national-intellectual-property-strategy)).

summary: The [data protection authority](2026-07-23-mozambique-government-preparing-personal-data-protection-law) exists only in the draft law, and donor funding for standing it up was cut from US$18m to US$11m in January 2026.
developments:
No authority has been established: it is provided for in the draft only, with a two-tier commission and agency in the September 2025 version ([review](2025-09-23 Review of Mozambique's Proposed Personal Data Protection Law), [preparation](2026-07-23-mozambique-government-preparing-personal-data-protection-law)).

A December 2025 diagnostic recommended creating one ([diagnostic](2025-12-09-world-bank-data-governance-mozambique-final)). In January 2026 the funder cut the project subcomponent covering cybersecurity and data protection from US$18m to US$11m, stating that operationalising the Data Protection Office had been envisaged over six years and the remaining project period no longer allows it ([restructuring](2026-01-16-worldbank-mozambique-digital-acceleration-project-second-restructuring-paper)).

Four institutions exercise implied oversight between them, with coordination gaps ([inception](2025-06-19-uneca-intic-mozambique-data-governance-project-inception-report)).

summary: A [personal-data breach reporting platform](2026-02-06 Mozambique intros data breach platform) has taken reports since February 2026, operating with no data-protection statute behind it.
developments:
The platform launched as a pilot in February 2026 and takes reports of personal-data breaches, illicit content and cyber incidents ([platform](2026-02-06 Mozambique intros data breach platform), [update](2026-06-23 Bimonthly Update on Privacy in Africa (January & February 2026))).

No reporting volumes and no exit-from-pilot date are on record. A breach-reporting channel without a statute defining a breach, a controller's duty or a sanction is a useful thing built in the wrong order, and it is the country's only operating data-protection mechanism.

summary: A [data sharing agreement](2025-12-15-afghs-specimen-sharing-agreement-mozambique) under a bilateral health memorandum was published in full, requiring specimens and sequencing data within eight working days with advance consent to onward sharing.
developments:
The agreement was signed at Washington in December 2025 and published as a treaty record ([agreement](2025-12-15-afghs-specimen-sharing-agreement-mozambique)).

Specimens, sequencing data and digital sequence information are to be shared within eight working days of a request, subject to approval by the national ethics, biosafety and security authority which shall not be unreasonably withheld, with advance consent to onward sharing with United States entities on after-the-fact notice and no cap on recipients ([assessment](2026-06-08-hrw-human-rights-assessment-afghs-bilateral-health-agreements), [memorandum](2025-12-15-afghs-mou-mozambique)).

The terms are looser than a comparable country's on transfer time and tighter on consent. It is the country's only published cross-border data transfer instrument, and it runs in a jurisdiction with no data protection statute ([complaint](2026-04-02-public-citizen-v-department-of-state-foia-complaint)).

summary: Two [memoranda with Angola](2026-06-23-angola-mozambique-space-and-digital-cooperation-mous) and one on [digital identity with Ethiopia](2026-04-28 Mozambique taps Ethiopia's digital ID expertise in DPI partnership) were signed in 2026, and the [United Nations cybercrime convention](2025-12-16-end-impunity-cybercrime-minister-clubofmozambique) was signed but not ratified.
developments:
The two Angolan memoranda cover space-sector cooperation and communications, information technology, information and meteorology ([memoranda](2026-06-23-angola-mozambique-space-and-digital-cooperation-mous)).

The Ethiopian memorandum, signed in Addis Ababa on an initial three-year term, covers digital-identity platforms and authentication, pilot projects, government-system interoperability, technical training and joint cybersecurity policy; its text is not held ([memorandum](2026-04-27-mozambique-ethiopia-mou-digital-identity-clubofmozambique), [account](2026-04-28 Mozambique taps Ethiopia's digital ID expertise in DPI partnership)).

The cybercrime convention was signed at Hanoi in October 2025 and the ratification request was still to be submitted to parliament in December 2025, with no update since ([signature](2025-12-16-end-impunity-cybercrime-minister-clubofmozambique)).

summary: The [regional convention on cyber security and personal data protection](2025-06-19-uneca-intic-mozambique-data-governance-project-inception-report) was ratified in 2019 and no domestic statute gives effect to it.
developments:
The ratification is recorded in a single line of a consultancy inception report; no month, instrument of ratification or deposit date is held ([ratification](2025-06-19-uneca-intic-mozambique-data-governance-project-inception-report)).

Seven years on, the domestic data-protection statute the convention obliges has not been enacted, so what the country has harmonised is its international commitment and not its law.

summary: A [cross-border fibre interconnector](2026-02-23 Zambia and Mozambique launch fibre-optic interconnector at Chanida–Cassacatiza border) to Zambia was commissioned in February 2026, and a [Nacala to Lobito submarine cable](2026-06-22-chapo-pledges-5g-district-capitals-2027-clubofmozambique) is in design.
developments:
The interconnector links Zambia's national backbone to Mozambique's submarine cable network and was commissioned in February 2026; no capacity, cost or traffic figure is stated by either government ([interconnector](2026-02-23 Zambia and Mozambique launch fibre-optic interconnector at Chanida–Cassacatiza border)).

The President stated that a Nacala to Lobito submarine cable is in the design phase; the only held statement on the project is one sentence in that speech, with no route length, cost, financier or in-service date ([cable](2026-06-22-chapo-pledges-5g-district-capitals-2027-clubofmozambique)).

summary: An [electronic government systems interoperability regulation](2025-12-05-prioritizes-data-governance-digital-sovereignty-techafricanews) was reviewed in December 2025, stated to set standards for integrating public information systems.
developments:
The review rests on a single account of institute remarks and the regulation text is not held ([review](2025-12-05-prioritizes-data-governance-digital-sovereignty-techafricanews)).

No standards register, conformance requirement or list of systems bound by it is published, so the base records that an interoperability rule exists and cannot say what it requires.

summary: A [free public device-identity lookup](2026-08-04-incm-comunicado-plataforma-consulta-imei) against the global device registry went live in August 2026, with no enforcement attached.
developments:
The regulator opened public lookup against the industry association's global device registry on 4 August 2026 ([notice](2026-08-04-incm-comunicado-plataforma-consulta-imei), [platform](2026-08-04-mozambique-incm-public-imei-database)).

It is verification only: no type approval, import control, blocking regime or penalty is attached, so a buyer can check a handset and the state cannot act on what the check shows.

progress: Mixed, blocking and interception powers struck down by the constitutional court while the government states it will seek the same end by another route
summary: The [telecommunications traffic control regulations](2026-07-29-mocambique-conselho-constitucional-acordao-6-cc-2026) were declared unconstitutional in July 2026, and the government said days later it [would pursue the same powers another way](2026-08-04-mozambique-government-response-cc-ruling-telecom-traffic).
developments:
The decree, approved in October 2025 and in force from December, gave powers to suspend or block services, compel call and internet-protocol detail records, issue binding technical norms and intervene in operator networks without consent ([decree](2025-12-16-mocambique-decreto-48-2025-controlo-trafego-telecomunicacoes)).

Judgment 6/CC/2026 of 29 July 2026 voided those provisions ([judgment](2026-07-29-mocambique-conselho-constitucional-acordao-6-cc-2026)). The ground was organic unconstitutionality, so the powers remain available to the assembly by statute.

The government stated on 4 August 2026 that it respects the ruling and will seek the same end by another route, naming no bill, instrument or timetable ([response](2026-08-03-club-of-mozambique-government-respects-telecom-traffic-ruling), [statement](2026-08-04-mozambique-government-response-cc-ruling-telecom-traffic)).

progress: Mixed, a reformed universal access levy against three digital agencies with no capital allocation at all
summary: The [2026 appropriations](2026-01-01-moz-2026-52a001641) give three digital agencies no capital line, and the new [Cyber Security Fund](2026-07-01-mocambique-lei-13-2026-seguranca-cibernetica-lei-14-2026-crimes-ciberneticos) has no budget line either.
developments:
The universal access fund regulation of May 2025 caps spending at 55 per cent infrastructure expansion, 14 per cent digital inclusion, 14 per cent broadcasting, 14 per cent operating costs and 3 per cent innovation, with the levy stated by the regulator at 1 per cent of each licensed entity's gross revenue ([regulation](2025-05-16-mocambique-decreto-11-2025-regulamento-fundo-servico-acesso-universal), [annual report](2024-01-01-incm-relatorio-regulacao-comunicacoes-2024)).

The 2026 final maps give the ICT institute MZN 73,636,370, the identification directorate MZN 230,819,650 and the statistics institute MZN 211,296,440 centrally, none of the three with a capital allocation, and salaries are between 77.5 and 93.2 per cent of each ([maps](2026-01-01-moz-2026-52a001641)).

The Cyber Security Fund is provided for in statute from July 2026 with state appropriations among its revenue lines, and no line for it appears in the 2026 budget ([fund](2026-07-01-mocambique-lei-13-2026-seguranca-cibernetica-lei-14-2026-crimes-ciberneticos)).

summary: The [digital acceleration project](2026-06-24-worldbank-mdap-p176459-isr-seq8) had disbursed US$83.88m of US$200m by June 2026, beside a [governance and economy project](2025-02-28-worldbank-mozambique-edge-restructuring-paper-res00782) and a [rural energy and broadband project](2021-12-14-wb-moz-002-sustainable-energy-and-broadband-access-in).
developments:
The digital acceleration project reached US$83,880,000 disbursed of US$200m in June 2026 and its overall implementation progress was upgraded to moderately satisfactory, while its data-protection-regulations indicator remains at zero of a target of two ([supervision](2026-06-24-worldbank-mdap-p176459-isr-seq8), [restructuring](2026-01-16-worldbank-mozambique-digital-acceleration-project-second-restructuring-paper)).

The governance and economy project stood at US$65.59m disbursed of a net US$137.85m in February 2025, with progress and implementation both rated moderately unsatisfactory ([project](2025-02-28-worldbank-mozambique-edge-restructuring-paper-res00782)).

A rural energy and broadband project had disbursed US$190,819,278 of US$343m by June 2026 ([rural project](2021-12-14-wb-moz-002-sustainable-energy-and-broadband-access-in)), and a separate digital programme committed EUR 22.5m in 2022 with nothing disbursed on the published record ([programme](2022-01-01-ec-moz-002-vamoz-digital)).

summary: A [US$132m network modernisation facility](2020-01-01-eximbank-cn-moz-002-modernization-and-expansion-of-the-national) was 57 per cent complete in 2023 with no completion report, and a [second US$200m facility](2025-01-01-eximbank-cn-moz-005-tmcel-telecommunications-network-second-expansion-financing) has not been signed.
developments:
The first facility was committed in 2020 and stood at 57 per cent complete in September 2023 with completion expected in May 2024 ([facility](2020-01-01-eximbank-cn-moz-002-modernization-and-expansion-of-the-national)); no completion or delivery report is held and no signed loan agreement is public ([facility](2020-01-01-eximbank-cn-moz-002-modernization-and-expansion-of-the-national)).

A second expansion financing of about US$200m was reported secured in April 2025 with terms undisclosed, and no signing, drawdown or works have been reported ([second facility](2025-01-01-eximbank-cn-moz-005-tmcel-telecommunications-network-second-expansion-financing)); the record rests on a single low-tier press source and an estimated amount ([second facility](2025-01-01-eximbank-cn-moz-005-tmcel-telecommunications-network-second-expansion-financing)).

progress: Mixed, 5G licensed with 2027 coverage deadlines while six administrative posts and 209 localities still have no service at all
summary: [5G spectrum was assigned](2026-06-24-incm-awards-5g-licences-mozambique-operators) to three operators in June 2026 with a [provincial-capital deadline of June 2027](2026-08-25-diario-economico-mocambique-5g-capitais-provinciais-incm), against [209 of 1,222 localities uncovered](2024-01-01-incm-relatorio-regulacao-comunicacoes-2024).
developments:
Licences were awarded to the three operators in June 2026 by administrative consignment rather than auction, covering 5G and 4G expansion; one group reports 210 MHz assigned to its Mozambican operator for US$56m with payment and licence terms still being finalised ([award](2026-06-24-incm-awards-5g-licences-mozambique-operators), [revenue](2026-07-27-vodafone-africa-q1-fy27-service-revenue)).

The licences carry a deadline of June 2027 for 5G in every provincial capital, with 4G obligations reaching border and rural areas in a later phase; two operators put on record that many target localities have no grid electricity, roads or backhaul ([terms](2026-08-25-diario-economico-mocambique-5g-capitais-provinciais-incm)).

The regulator's 2024 report has 6 of 453 administrative posts and 209 of 1,222 localities uncovered, at 82.9 per cent locality coverage, with no later figure published ([coverage](2024-01-01-incm-relatorio-regulacao-comunicacoes-2024)).

summary: A [public broadband coverage portal](2026-07-23-mozambique-portail-national-haut-debit) went live in July 2026 letting anyone query operator coverage and speeds by location, with a public gap-reporting channel.
developments:
The geospatial platform was built with commercial mapping software and publishes operator coverage and speeds queryable by location, with a channel for the public to report gaps ([portal](2026-07-23-mozambique-portail-national-haut-debit)).

No usage or gap-report figures have been published. The portal maps what is available rather than what is used, and no national internet penetration figure is published alongside it.

summary: A standard data package fell from [9.4 per cent of monthly income per head in 2022 to 2.67 per cent in March 2026](2026-08-10-mozambique-national-broadband-map-incm-portal), on the funder's own figures.
developments:
The figures were released with the national coverage map and are the World Bank project's own; the basket behind the standard package is not defined in the record held ([figures](2026-08-10-mozambique-national-broadband-map-incm-portal)).

A fall of that size in four years is the largest single improvement recorded for the country in this base, and it is the one measure here that a household would feel directly.

summary: The incumbent's modernisation facility covers [7,600 km of fibre and capacity from 10 to 400 Gbit/s](2020-01-01-eximbank-cn-moz-002-modernization-and-expansion-of-the-national), last reported 57 per cent complete in 2023.
developments:
The scope is 1,350 antennas, 7,600 km of fibre and capacity raised from 10 to 400 Gbit/s, at 57 per cent complete in September 2023 with completion expected in May 2024 ([facility](2020-01-01-eximbank-cn-moz-002-modernization-and-expansion-of-the-national)).

No completion or delivery report has entered the base since. It is the only national backbone build on record, and its last measured position is three years old.

summary: A [subsea cable southern extension](2025-09-01-dare1-extension-techafricanews) announced in 2025 plans a Mozambican landing, with work from 2026 and service from 2028.
developments:
The extension plans landings in Tanzania, Mozambique, Madagascar and South Africa, interconnecting at Mombasa, with the Mombasa to Durban route estimated at 3,200 to 3,500 km ([extension](2025-09-01-dare1-extension-techafricanews)); no construction start was confirmed by August 2026 ([extension](2025-09-01-dare1-extension-techafricanews)).

No capacity, price or utilisation figure for the country's existing international bandwidth is held, so the addition is on record and the base it adds to is not.

summary: The [national internet exchange](2026-08-08-mozix-mozambique-internet-exchange-about) carries 143 Gbps of cumulative member port capacity across eighteen peers, and opened a [second point of presence](2025-05-15-mozambique-internet-exchange-new-pop-digital-realty-maputo) in a carrier-neutral Maputo facility in May 2025.
developments:
The exchange is operated by the national university's computer centre in Maputo, founded in May 2002, with eighteen peers on its own site and 143 Gbps of cumulative member port capacity ([exchange](2026-08-08-mozix-mozambique-internet-exchange-about)).

A second point of presence opened at a carrier-neutral Maputo data centre hosting more than fifteen network operators in May 2025, when the exchange reported peak traffic above 150 Gbps across nineteen peering members and about 35 per cent of the country's internet traffic routed through domestic exchanges ([point of presence](2025-05-15-mozambique-internet-exchange-new-pop-digital-realty-maputo)).

Member port capacity is an upper bound on what could be exchanged at one time and not measured traffic; no autonomous systems joined or left over the tracked period and the exchange's own peering database record has been stale since 2016 ([tracker](2026-07-01-isoc-pulse-ixp-tracker-mozix)). The peer count falls between the 2025 and 2026 accounts and neither explains it.

summary: [Low-orbit service is live](2026-01-01 Starlink Partners with Airtel & Vodacom From Rival to Ally) with an operator backhaul partnership, [donated terminals went to flood centres](2026-02-19-starlink-vodacom-flood-response-clubofmozambique), and [trials of an Angolan satellite](2026-08-25-tmcel-angosat2-satellite-trials-itweb) began in August 2026.
developments:
The low-orbit service is live, with an operator backhaul and equipment-resale partnership; no licence date, subscriber count or terminal count is held ([service](2026-01-01 Starlink Partners with Airtel & Vodacom From Rival to Ally), [deployment](2026-02-19-starlink-vodacom-flood-response-clubofmozambique)).

Donated terminals were deployed by the regulator with open access at flood accommodation and coordination centres in February 2026, plus four operator connectivity kits at four named locations; the terminal count is not stated ([terminals](2026-02-19-starlink-vodacom-flood-response-clubofmozambique)).

The state operator began proof-of-concept testing of the Angolan satellite in August 2026 as a step towards a commercial agreement, implementing a bilateral memorandum of June 2026; no commercial terms are published ([trials](2026-08-25-tmcel-angosat2-satellite-trials-itweb)).

summary: The [national count](2025-03-29-pm-opens-vodacom-data-centre-clubofmozambique) stands at seventeen or eighteen on one 2025 speech, above a [400-rack Tier III facility](2026-08-08-raxio-mozambique-mz1-data-centre-specification) and a [US$25m operator centre](2025-03-31 Vodacom opens data center in Maputo, Mozambique).
developments:
The only national count is a figure given by the Prime Minister in March 2025, which two accounts of the same sentence report as seventeen and as eighteen; nothing later has been published and the university facility and two announced availability zones appear in no national count ([count](2025-03-29-pm-opens-vodacom-data-centre-clubofmozambique), [account](2025-03-31 Vodacom opens data center in Maputo, Mozambique)).

The independent carrier-neutral facility at Beluluane is Tier III certified with 400 racks, 2,000 square metres of white space and 3 MW of information technology power, indirect adiabatic cooling at a stated power usage effectiveness of 1.3, and eight connectivity providers terminating fibre into two meet-me rooms ([facility](2026-08-08-raxio-mozambique-mz1-data-centre-specification)).

An operator's Tier III centre at Matola opened in March 2025 at US$25m with direct access to a subsea cable ([centre](2025-03-31 Vodacom opens data center in Maputo, Mozambique)), and a network operator announced co-location into the independent facility in July 2026 ([co-location](2026-07-23-raxio-afr-ix-data-centres-angola-mozambique)).

progress: Mixed, a new university facility in service while the state's own data centre is described as capable and underused
summary: A [university data centre](2026-08-11-uem-eduardo-mondlane-university-inaugurates-data-centre) opened in August 2026, while the [state data centre](2025-07-24-intic-joanguete-podemos-falar-da-inteligencia-artificial-sem-data-center) is described as technically capable but underused.
developments:
The university facility entered service on 11 August 2026 with about fourteen times the storage of the server room it replaces, precision cooling, redundant systems and hardened physical security, designated to help underpin the country-code domain and the internet exchange and intended to carry research, cloud and artificial-intelligence services; it is donor-financed with no amount stated ([inauguration](2026-08-11-uem-eduardo-mondlane-university-inaugurates-data-centre), [account](2026-08-03-uem-centro-de-dados-transformacao-digital)).

The state facility is in operation and, on an account published by the regulator, technically capable but underused, with state institutions not digitising and structuring their data into it in the absence of a national digitisation and systems-integration strategy; capacity, tenants and hosting arrangements are not stated, and nothing on record establishes where government systems are hosted ([assessment](2025-07-24-intic-joanguete-podemos-falar-da-inteligencia-artificial-sem-data-center), [bandwidth](2025-05-08-intic-inteligencia-artificial-desafios-e-oportunidades-para-mocambique)).

summary: The [data-centre regulation](2026-02-18-approval-data-center-regulation) sets resilience and continuity obligations but names no power requirement, and the [university facility](2026-08-03-uem-centro-de-dados-transformacao-digital) is the only one in the base whose power design is described.
developments:
The data-centre regulation approved by Decree 71/2025 sets security obligations and requirements for resilience, continuity of service and physical and cyber security, and requires civil liability insurance against force majeure; no power, grid-resilience or energy-efficiency requirement is named ([regulation](2026-02-18-approval-data-center-regulation)).

The university facility's power design is grid supply with integrated photovoltaic generation and a generator as redundancy, named by the minister as the reason interruption risk falls; capacity, generation and consumption figures are not stated ([design](2026-08-03-uem-centro-de-dados-transformacao-digital)). It is the only facility in the base with its power design described.

The utility's published industrial schedule gives medium voltage at 4.78 metical a kilowatt-hour plus fixed and capacity charges and high voltage at 4.70, negotiable; no data-centre-specific supply arrangement is published ([tariffs](2026-08-08-edm-electricity-tariffs-mozambique)).

progress: Mixed, a year of destruction and hydrological shortfall against a stated investment for the next one
summary: The [state utility](2026-07-01-vandalism-cyclones-edm-performance-2025) lost supply and revenue through 2025 to unrest, cyclones and hydrological deficit, and states it will spend US$82 million in 2026 on grid expansion.
developments:
The utility's 2025 annual report attributes the year's performance to civil unrest and infrastructure destruction, cyclone damage, hydrological deficits limiting domestic generation and export, and the unavailability of the Maputo thermal plant; it records customer cancellations and reductions in contracted capacity and emergency repair spending ([report](2026-07-01-vandalism-cyclones-edm-performance-2025)).

Against that it states an investment of US$82 million in 2026 for grid expansion, targeting 420,000 new residential connections ([report](2026-07-01-vandalism-cyclones-edm-performance-2025)).

A national control centre for energy was committed at EUR 8,008,000 in 2022 and nothing had been disbursed at the last read in June 2026 ([commitment](2022-01-01-ec-moz-007-national-control-centre-for-energy)). No outage series, availability figure or reserve-margin measure is published, so the utility's own account is the whole of the record.

summary: [Solar systems were specified for all 60](2025-10-20-60-new-mobile-stations-rural-connectivity-techafricanews) of the rural mobile stations awarded in October 2025, with no installed capacity or commissioning date stated.
developments:
Solar energy systems are specified to power all sixty sites, which was not in the tender notice; no installed capacity, supplier or commissioning date is stated ([specification](2025-10-20-60-new-mobile-stations-rural-connectivity-techafricanews)).

It is the only held statement of the power design for the rural build, and the only rural electrification evidence in the country's digital record: the base holds no national electrification rate against which to set it.

summary: The [country-code domain](2020-09-10-decreto-82-2020-regulamento-do-uso-do-dominio-mz-mocambique) is managed by the regulator with no operator named and no registration volumes published, and [CloudGov](2020-08-13-inage-cloudgov-sistema-de-armazenamento-de-arquivos) has had no account since 2020.
developments:
A 2020 decree vests management and operation of the domain and its official subdomains in the regulator and permits delegation of the technical aspects by public tender or direct award; no operator is named in the text, the government subdomain is compulsory for every body in the structure of government, and no registration count is published anywhere in the base ([decree](2020-09-10-decreto-82-2020-regulamento-do-uso-do-dominio-mz-mocambique)).

A government-wide storage, sync and share platform was announced in 2020 as a pandemic response and described as in rollout across public-administration institutions; no later account, institution count or usage figure is held ([platform](2020-08-13-inage-cloudgov-sistema-de-armazenamento-de-arquivos)).

summary: [173,770 attacks and 1,061 criminal cases](2026-04-16-records-173000-cyberattacks-2024-clubofmozambique) were recorded in 2024, and the national response team detected [5,654 ransomware attempts](2026-08-06-mozambique-intic-ransomware-campaign) in the first seven months of 2026.
developments:
The communications minister gave parliament 173,770 attacks and 1,061 criminal cases for 2024 against 912 cases in 2023, and 36,330 attacks for the first half of 2025 ([figures](2026-04-16-records-173000-cyberattacks-2024-clubofmozambique), [account](2026-06-22-fast-tracks-ai-cyber-strategy-itweb)). These are government detection counts with no published methodology, so the series is not safely comparable.

The national response team detected 5,654 ransomware infection attempts between January and July 2026, disclosed at the launch of a prevention campaign ([attempts](2026-08-06-mozambique-intic-ransomware-campaign)); these are attempts detected rather than incidents suffered, and no comparable earlier period is published ([attempts](2026-08-06-mozambique-intic-ransomware-campaign)).

summary: A [successor cyber strategy](2026-08-19-revistatempo-mozambique-intic-finlandia-estrategia-ciberseguranca-2026-2030) is in preparation and a [national risk assessment](2025-05-02-intic-relatorio-avaliacao-nacional-riscos-ciberneticos-infraestruturas-criticas) rates nineteen of twenty-nine critical systems very high risk, against a [regional index placing](2024-10-22-cenario-seguranca-cibernetica-palop) the country first among its language group.
developments:
The 2021-2025 policy ran six pillars and twenty-five projects; its successor is under revision, adding safeguards against artificial-intelligence risks, with no adoption date ([revision](2026-08-19-revistatempo-mozambique-intic-finlandia-estrategia-ciberseguranca-2026-2030), [predecessor](2021-12-31-mozambique-resolucao-69-2021-politica-estrategia-nacional-seguranca-cibernetica)). Its period ended before its successor was drafted.

The incident response team was created in statute and seated in the ICT institute, which named consolidating it the immediate priority; fourteen national specialists hold an international maturity certification ([team](2026-07-23-mozambique-intic-cybersecurity-seminar-laws-13-14-2026-csirt)).

The first national cyber risk assessment, published in May 2025 on a foreign methodology, rates 19 of 29 systems across 18 institutions very high risk, 6 high and 4 moderate; it names no operator and no system, so it publishes a risk distribution without a register of what is at risk ([assessment](2025-05-02-intic-relatorio-avaliacao-nacional-riscos-ciberneticos-infraestruturas-criticas)).

A Cyber Security Fund is provided for at articles 67 to 71 of the new statute, financed by a levy on licensed providers and state appropriations; its operating rules are left to a regulation not yet made ([fund](2026-07-01-mocambique-lei-13-2026-seguranca-cibernetica-lei-14-2026-crimes-ciberneticos)).

The ICT institute reports the country [first among the Portuguese-speaking African countries in the 2024 Global Cybersecurity Index](2024-10-22-cenario-seguranca-cibernetica-palop), up on 2020, with capacity development the pillar still to improve; no score or overall rank is given in the account held.

summary: An [X-Road interoperability platform](2026-05-25-tender-mobile-digital-identity-signature-clubofmozambique) is described as under implementation, and a [single unified government database](2026-03-16-sets-up-agency-digital-transformation-biometricupdate) is named as an agency responsibility.
developments:
The platform is named as currently being implemented in a May 2026 tender document, with no operator, go-live date or list of connected agencies on record ([platform](2026-05-25-tender-mobile-digital-identity-signature-clubofmozambique), [tender](2026-05-26-seeks-partner-mobile-digital-id-esignature-biometricupdate)).

A single unified government database is named as a responsibility of the digital transformation agency, with no design, scope, host or timetable published ([database](2026-03-16-sets-up-agency-digital-transformation-biometricupdate)).

Both are known only through documents about something else, which is the state of the exchange layer here: named in other people's paperwork and never described in its own.

summary: [Biometric identity and access management](2026-02-24 BIO-key and RunLevel Deploy Biometric IAM Across Mozambique's National Payments Network) is being deployed into the national payments switch, having previously run in a single bank.
developments:
A multi-year deployment agreement was announced in February 2026 taking biometric identity and access management from a single national bank deployment into the national payments network ([deployment](2026-02-24 BIO-key and RunLevel Deploy Biometric IAM Across Mozambique's National Payments Network)).

The account is the vendor's, with no completion date or participating-bank count. It is the only case in the base of the country's identity layer reaching into another sector's infrastructure.

summary: [Updated civil identification regulations](2026-06-03-cabinet-approves-new-id-card-regulations-clubofmozambique) were approved in 2026 governing collection, processing and retention, and the [biometric passport](2026-07-29-jornal-noticias-senami-inovacao-tecnologica-atendimento) takes applications by electronic pre-booking.
developments:
The regulations under the 2022 identification law were updated and approved by the Council of Ministers, governing collection, processing, management and retention of civil identification data and standardising issuance; the instrument is not held and its provisions rest on a spokesperson's description ([regulations](2026-06-03-cabinet-approves-new-id-card-regulations-clubofmozambique), [framework](2026-07-27-mozambique-national-id-legal-framework-dnic)).

The biometric passport is in issue with applications submitted by electronic pre-booking, named as the principal documentary-security measure at the migration service's anniversary; no dates, volumes or coverage figures are given ([passport](2026-07-29-jornal-noticias-senami-inovacao-tecnologica-atendimento)).

summary: [856,101 identity cards](2026-07-23-clubofmozambique-dnic-identity-cards-first-semester) were produced in the first half of 2026, up from 730,527, of which [297,470 were issued free](2026-07-28-mozambique-free-id-and-birth-certificate-issuance-extended-2027).
developments:
Production ran at 856,101 cards on 813,307 applications in the first half of 2026, against 730,527 on 677,305 applications a year earlier ([production](2026-07-23-clubofmozambique-dnic-identity-cards-first-semester)); the figures are the directorate spokesperson's with no published series behind them ([production](2026-07-23-clubofmozambique-dnic-identity-cards-first-semester)).

Free first issuance of the identity card, birth certificate and personal certificate was extended to 2027 and widened to children and adults alike, with 297,470 free cards issued in the first half of 2026 ([extension](2026-07-28-mozambique-free-id-and-birth-certificate-issuance-extended-2027)); neither the 2027 end month nor the deadline replaced is stated ([extension](2026-07-28-mozambique-free-id-and-birth-certificate-issuance-extended-2027)).

summary: A [national mobile digital identity and electronic signature infrastructure](2026-05-25-tender-mobile-digital-identity-signature-clubofmozambique) went to tender in May 2026, with partner discussions opened in August.
developments:
The digital transformation agency floated a tender in May 2026 for a national mobile digital identity and electronic signature infrastructure ([tender](2026-05-25-tender-mobile-digital-identity-signature-clubofmozambique), [partner search](2026-05-26-seeks-partner-mobile-digital-id-esignature-biometricupdate)).

The ICT institute opened discussions with a local partner in August 2026 on a platform extending digital identity, advanced digital signatures and public key infrastructure into a national digital trust layer; it follows a February 2026 memorandum with a foreign institute covering credentialing, auditing, training and technical assistance for operating a root certification authority ([discussions](2026-08-25-mozambique-tablu-tech-digital-trust-biometricupdate)).

summary: [Biometric SIM registration](2024-01-18 Mozambique to Require Biometric Card Registration for Cellphone Users) became compulsory in 2024 with blocking from 2025, and nothing has entered the base on the regime since.
developments:
Registration was optional from a pilot in January 2024, compulsory in the second half of that year and subject to blocking from 2025, as described at the time ([regime](2024-01-18 Mozambique to Require Biometric Card Registration for Cellphone Users)).

No later account is held and no registration, blocking or enforcement figures exist in the base at all. Nothing has entered it on this regime for over two years, which for a compulsory nationwide identity-linked measure is the notable fact.

summary: A [National Payments System Law](2026-06-13-cybercrime-cybersecurity-nps-laws-signed-clubofmozambique) replaced the 2008 regime in July 2026, and a [notice](2026-06-02-mocambique-aviso-2-gbm-2026-rede-unica-pagamentos) makes switch connection mandatory with sixty-minute outage reporting.
developments:
The law was enacted in July 2026, extending central bank inspection and supervision over electronic-money institutions and new payment service providers; the official text is not held and its provisions rest on secondary accounts ([law](2026-06-13-cybercrime-cybersecurity-nps-laws-signed-clubofmozambique), [passage](2026-04-15-national-payments-system-law-approved-parliament-clubofmozambique)).

The notice makes connection to the single payments network mandatory to offer electronic payment products, with three months to migrate existing terminals, any unavailability lasting more than ten minutes reported within sixty minutes, annual recovery testing due 31 March and an annual incident-framework review ([notice](2026-06-02-mocambique-aviso-2-gbm-2026-rede-unica-pagamentos), [reporting](2026-06-16-financial-institutions-60-minutes-report-failures-clubofmozambique)).

summary: An [instant payment system](2026-02-25-mocambique-aviso-1-gbm-2026-sistema-pagamentos-instantaneos) entered production in March 2026 with free interbank person-to-person transfers, and [daily transfers tripled](2026-07-30-mozambique-metix-instant-payments-11000-daily-transfers) to more than 11,000.
developments:
The system runs around the clock over bank applications, websites and short codes, operated by the interbank company with wallet-operator participation mandatory and free interbank person-to-person transfers for individuals; the governing notice sets daily limits of 200,000 metical for individuals and 500,000 for legal persons and a twenty-five second fund-availability ceiling ([notice](2026-02-25-mocambique-aviso-1-gbm-2026-sistema-pagamentos-instantaneos), [launch](2026-03-16-central-bank-launches-metix-clubofmozambique)).

Daily transfers passed 11,000 by July 2026, a tripling since production entry in March ([volumes](2026-07-30-mozambique-metix-instant-payments-11000-daily-transfers)). Against a base of more than twenty-five million wallet accounts, that is a system working and barely used.

The switch behind it is not new: the interbank company was established in 2011 to give all payment service providers a single clearance platform, launched a bank-to-bank instant payment system in 2012 and a cross-domain system in 2022, before which processors and switches were not interconnected, pricing was opaque and interoperability between bank accounts and mobile money was limited ([case study](2025-11-01-siips-2025-simo-mozambique-case-study)).

summary: More than [US$14.4m has been paid to nearly 246,000 health workers](2026-08-11-who-mozambique-mobile-money-health-campaigns) by mobile money since 2024, replacing cash for vaccination and emergency campaigns.
developments:
The cumulative figure to August 2026 is more than US$14.4m paid to nearly 246,000 health workers and volunteers, replacing cash and giving funders a full digital transaction record ([payments](2026-08-11-who-mozambique-mobile-money-health-campaigns)).

The figures are the agency's own, the payments run through commercial mobile-money operators the account does not name, and no per-campaign breakdown or failure rate is published. It is the country's only recorded government-to-person digital payment stream, and it is run by an international agency rather than by the state.

summary: An [online tax clearance certificate](2026-07-31-mozambique-tax-clearance-certificate-online-portal-contribuinte) went live in August 2026 with a ten working-day ceiling, and a [tax amendment on wallet-agent commissions](2025-08-25-irps-tax-mobile-money-agents-clubofmozambique) is in preparation.
developments:
The certificate is requested through the taxpayer portal and issued within a maximum of ten working days, with a published electronic complaints address; the authority's own communique is not held ([certificate](2026-07-31-mozambique-tax-clearance-certificate-online-portal-contribuinte)).

An amendment on the taxation of mobile-money agent commissions is still in preparation, with taxation already proceeding under the existing framework and 787 wallet agents registered for tax numbers in the first half of 2025; no adoption, tabling or gazetting is held ([amendment](2025-08-25-irps-tax-mobile-money-agents-clubofmozambique)).

progress: Mixed, wallet accounts and agents growing sharply while card terminals fell and the inclusion index did not move
summary: Mobile money reached [1,313 accounts per thousand adults](2026-07-24-clubofmozambique-atms-pos-lose-ground-mobile-money) in 2025 and [access points rose 36 per cent](2026-07-24-clubofmozambique-atms-pos-lose-ground-mobile-money), while the [inclusion index held at 36.4](2026-07-24-clubofmozambique-atms-pos-lose-ground-mobile-money).
developments:
Mobile money holdings rose from 1,093 to 1,313 accounts per thousand adults and bank accounts from 330 to 337 between 2024 and 2025, with women's mobile money holding rising from 924 to 1,144 ([accounts](2026-07-24-clubofmozambique-atms-pos-lose-ground-mobile-money)).

Non-bank agents rose from 315,005 to 446,604 while cash machines fell from 1,391 to 1,383 and card terminals from 35,486 to 32,236, giving 482,359 access points in total, up 36 per cent ([access points](2026-07-24-clubofmozambique-atms-pos-lose-ground-mobile-money)); the central bank attributes the terminal fall to decommissioning of inactive devices ([access points](2026-07-24-clubofmozambique-atms-pos-lose-ground-mobile-money)).

The national inclusion index held at 36.4 points across the same year ([index](2026-07-24-clubofmozambique-atms-pos-lose-ground-mobile-money)), against a strategy targeting 60 per cent of adults with a bank account by 2031 ([strategy](2025-08-06-e-money-accounts-109pct-adult-population-clubofmozambique)).

summary: The [electronic civil registration system](2024-01-01-mozambique-crvs-law-policy-summary) established by the revised Civil Registration Code runs behind a [free birth registration campaign](2026-03-31-government-launches-free-birth-registration-clubofmozambique) targeting about seven million people to the end of 2026.
developments:
The national civil registration system is administered by the justice ministry through the national directorate of registries and notary services, established by the Civil Registration Code as revised in 2018 and integrated with the national identity and health systems; the Code mandates registration of all vital events, compulsory free birth registration within 120 days, and electronic transmission of data to the statistics institute ([code](2024-01-01-mozambique-crvs-law-policy-summary), [portal](2024-01-01-e-sircev-portal)).

The campaign launched in March 2026 and runs to 31 December, targeting about seven million people at 25,000 registrations a day through up to 500 mobile brigades, with costs met by a donor-funded governance project ([campaign](2026-03-31-government-launches-free-birth-registration-clubofmozambique)); no mid-campaign total is on record ([campaign](2026-03-31-government-launches-free-birth-registration-clubofmozambique), [launch](2026-05-21-chapo-free-civil-registration-campaign-clubofmozambique)).

A tender for civil registration and population register services closed in February 2026, requiring bidders to show a US$7m or two US$4m track record and a US$90,000 bid security ([tender](2026-01-05-seeks-expert-services-mass-birth-id-registration-biometricupdate)); no award, contractor or contract value is established ([tender](2026-01-05-seeks-expert-services-mass-birth-id-registration-biometricupdate)).

Two earlier vital-statistics programmes closed fully disbursed at the end of 2023, at CAD 19.5m and CAD 6.5m ([first phase](2017-01-01-gac-moz-vital-stats-mnch-2017-vital-statistics-in-support-of-maternal), [second phase](2021-01-01-gac-moz-vital-stats-mnch-2021-vital-statistics-in-support-of-maternal)).

summary: The [land information system](2019-07-19-fnds-sigit-lims-review-final-report) had recorded 563,765 land-use right requests, 77 per cent processed and 68 per cent delivered to beneficiaries.
developments:
The system digitises land-use right application processing, with 563,765 requests recorded, 77 per cent processed and 68 per cent delivered ([system](2019-07-19-fnds-sigit-lims-review-final-report)).

The figures come from a 2019 review report and nothing later is held, so the country's only quantified registry position is seven years old and the gap between processed and delivered is the part worth watching.

summary: [74 per cent of legal-entity registrations](2026-06-29-74pct-legal-entity-registration-electronic-clubofmozambique) were submitted electronically by June 2026, on the justice minister's figure.
developments:
The share was stated by the minister at an international legal forum, with no published series behind it ([share](2026-06-29-74pct-legal-entity-registration-electronic-clubofmozambique)).

No absolute registration count, processing time or rejection rate is held. A three-quarters electronic share with no denominator is the shape of most of this unit's administrative evidence.

summary: A [biometric register of humanitarian-aid recipients](2026-08-12-mozambique-s-digital-humanitarian-response-system-set-for-october-launch) completed validation for national launch in October 2026, built to interoperate with the national social-support database.
developments:
Validation of the beneficiary and humanitarian assistance management system is complete, with national launch stated for October 2026 after a pilot at Beira, at a costed investment of about 20 million metical ([validation](2026-08-12-mozambique-s-digital-humanitarian-response-system-set-for-october-launch), [register](2026-08-09-mozambique-aid-recipient-digital-register)).

It is built to interoperate with the national social-support database so responders can see who has and has not received aid and duplicate or fictitious registrations are curbed. No data-protection basis, retention rule or enrolment target is published, and the country has no data-protection statute.

summary: A [national electronic medical record](2025-12-15-afghs-mou-mozambique) has a minimum viable version targeted for September 2026, under a [ten-year digital health strategy](2026-07-23-ictworks-african-national-digital-health-strategies-2026) and a [data-quality plan](2025-01-01-misau-plano-melhoria-qualidade-dados-2025-2029).
developments:
The government is owner and operator of the core integrated electronic medical record, its minimum viable version targeted for September 2026 with modules for registration, consultation, maternal and child health and two disease programmes; a foreign-built patient tracking system was to pass to Mozambican management by June 2026 and be retired once migrated, with laboratory, surveillance and logistics systems behind a health data exchange expected functional by the end of 2026 ([architecture](2025-12-15-afghs-mou-mozambique)).

That architecture is named in a United States instrument the government signed, and no Mozambican document naming these systems is held ([record](2025-12-15-state-moz-afghs-data-systems-2025-record)).

The country's first dedicated digital health strategy runs on a ten-year horizon and is known only through a dated reference directory ([strategy](2026-07-23-ictworks-african-national-digital-health-strategies-2026)); a five-year data-quality plan followed an assessment finding 9 per cent exact-match between records and facility registers ([plan](2025-01-01-misau-plano-melhoria-qualidade-dados-2025-2029)).

One hospital is running an inpatient system: Mavalane General Hospital in Maputo became the country's first digital hospital in December 2024, with a hospital health information system digitising admissions and inpatient care, which the implementing partner puts at about US$7.8 million a year in paper costs saved ([case study](2025-01-01-jembi-mozambique-case-study)). The saving is the partner's own estimate with no method stated, and no second hospital is named.

summary: A [2024 law on electronic processing](2026-06-29-74pct-legal-entity-registration-electronic-clubofmozambique) is named as the cornerstone of judicial modernisation, and two operating systems now sit under it — a [gender-violence case platform](2023-04-18-innovative-data-tool-gbv-survivors-mozambique) and [camera-based traffic enforcement](2025-12-11-south-korea-digital-road-violation-monitoring).
developments:
The statute has been in force since 7 June 2024 and was named by the justice minister in June 2026 as the cornerstone of judicial modernisation; its text is not held ([law](2026-06-29-74pct-legal-entity-registration-electronic-clubofmozambique)). No case-management system, filing volume, disposal rate or court coverage figure is held.

The interior ministry runs InfoViolencia through police departments, the country's first digital platform for gender-based violence case data, used at Integrated Services Centres and police stations, where a single registration form replaces printed forms and generates referral reports across health, justice and social services ([platform](2023-04-18-innovative-data-tool-gbv-survivors-mozambique)). No case volume, coverage or data-protection arrangement is published for a system holding case files on named survivors, and nothing on it after April 2023.

Camera-based traffic enforcement went live across Greater Maputo on 10 December 2025, detecting violations, processing offences and sending fines by text message, under an [approximately US$7 million Korean-funded programme](2025-12-11-south-korea-digital-road-violation-monitoring). The road transport institute states that legislative adjustment is still needed for digital issuance of fines ([system](2025-12-11-south-korea-digital-road-violation-monitoring)). No data-retention, image-handling or appeal arrangement is published.

summary: Construction began in August 2026 on a [one-stop border post](2026-08-17-aim-governo-moderniza-fronteira-ressano-garcia) at the South African frontier, with the two countries to exchange data and share systems.
developments:
Ground was broken on 17 August 2026 under an investment plan of about 980 million metical, one tranche for modernising the post's technological infrastructure and a second for a road freight terminal and express lanes ([works](2026-08-17-aim-governo-moderniza-fronteira-ressano-garcia), [account](2026-08-17-mznews-ressano-garcia-fronteira-paragem-unica)).

The design has the two countries' authorities exchanging data and sharing systems so that an exit registration on one side reaches the other. No completion date, system specification or data-sharing instrument is published, which for a cross-border personal-data exchange is the material omission.

summary: A [citizen portal](2026-08-04-governo-digitaliza-mais-de-cem-servicos-publicos-portal-do-cidadao) enters experimental phase with about 140 services inventoried, an [environmental licensing platform](2026-08-20-360mozambique-sgla-environmental-licensing-platform) launched, and a [two-hour notification certificate](2026-08-03-government-approves-regulation-certificates-low-risk-activities-two-hours) was decreed.
developments:
The citizen portal's prototype is being completed with an experimental phase due between late August and early September 2026, about 140 public services inventoried for gradual integration beginning with passports and driving licences; no budget, supplier, authentication method or data-protection arrangement is stated ([portal](2026-08-04-governo-digitaliza-mais-de-cem-servicos-publicos-portal-do-cidadao), [agency](2026-03-16-sets-up-agency-digital-transformation-biometricupdate)).

An end-to-end environmental licensing system launched in August 2026 carrying a permit from application through issuance into monitoring, audit and inspection ([platform](2026-08-20-360mozambique-sgla-environmental-licensing-platform), [upgrade](2026-08-18-integritymagazine-sgla-2-0-licenciamento-ambiental)).

A decree approved in August 2026 requires a prior-notification certificate within two hours and lets the applicant trade anyway if it does not issue, mandates automatic information-sharing between five state bodies and makes electronic signature equivalent to handwritten; the decree is not held and the account names no safeguard or oversight for the mandated exchange ([decree](2026-08-03-government-approves-regulation-certificates-low-risk-activities-two-hours)). One-stop desks with an online platform were already operating ([desks](2025-12-09-world-bank-data-governance-mozambique-final)).

A second, authenticated portal is already in service: the registries and notary service's [Portal do Utente](2024-01-01-portal-do-utente-srn) carries legal-entity, vehicle, civil, criminal and property registration, notarial acts and the central registries, with case tracking, appointment booking and a declaration channel for beneficial owners. No user or transaction figure is published for it.

summary: A [22-module municipal management suite](2026-08-08-cedsif-sistema-de-gestao-autarquica-e-sga-especificacao) was specified in August 2026, under a [memorandum across all 65 municipalities](2025-02-22-jornal-noticias-digitalizacao-moderniza-gestao-municipal-no-pais) with no delivery report.
developments:
The suite spans twenty-two interoperable modules covering finance and revenue, urban and land, licensing, waste, cemeteries, fleet, parking and policing; no deployment date or municipality count is published ([specification](2026-08-08-cedsif-sistema-de-gestao-autarquica-e-sga-especificacao)).

A municipal digital services programme was launched by memorandum across all sixty-five municipalities in February 2025, covering virtual secretariats, digital tax clearance, transparency tools and a national document management system, with no budget, delivery or progress report held ([programme](2025-02-22-jornal-noticias-digitalizacao-moderniza-gestao-municipal-no-pais)).

Existing municipal systems are older and narrower: a property-tax system built in 2009 for the capital and three further revenue systems, with no national rollout or count of municipalities using them established ([systems](2020-09-01-pdul-avaliacao-rapida-sistemas-informacao-gestao-financeira-municipal)).

summary: [149 localities and 418 schools](2026-08-18-agenceecofin-mozambique-300-localites-services-telecoms) were connected under the ministry's programme, against a stated target of up to 4,000 schools.
developments:
The connected counts and the targets are the communications ministry's own, given without a completion date: at least 300 localities, up to 4,000 schools and around 10,000 new access points ([programme](2026-08-18-agenceecofin-mozambique-300-localites-services-telecoms)).

At 418 schools the programme is about a tenth of the way to its own ceiling. No completion date, per-school service level or count of schools still unconnected is published.

summary: A [National Commission for Artificial Intelligence](2026-05-06-cnia-begins-advising-government-on-ai-clubofmozambique) began advising government in 2026, an [observatory](2026-08-18-mozambique-ai-cultural-creative-economy) is proposed, and the Prime Minister [warned on deepfakes in elections](2026-08-26-clubofmozambique-pm-ai-deepfakes-electoral-integrity).
developments:
The commission was created by decree of 10 March 2026 and is an advisory body under the Council of Ministers chaired by the communications minister with the defence and education ministers as vice-presidents, issuing opinions on policy, legal instruments, funding, research and workforce questions; the decree number is not stated in any held source ([commission](2026-05-06-cnia-begins-advising-government-on-ai-clubofmozambique), [framework](2026-03-27-builds-institutional-framework-digital-transformation-wearetech)).

A National Artificial Intelligence Observatory was named in August 2026 as expected to support transparency, build trust and measure impact; no establishing instrument, host, membership, funding or method is on record ([observatory](2026-08-18-mozambique-ai-cultural-creative-economy)).

The Prime Minister welcomed artificial intelligence while warning of the dangers of deepfakes in elections; no detection capability, electoral rule or platform obligation follows it ([statement](2026-08-26-clubofmozambique-pm-ai-deepfakes-electoral-integrity)).

summary: Mozambique is a [founding member of a world artificial-intelligence cooperation body](2026-07-27-clubofmozambique-waico-founding-member) and is [named as implementing a regulatory sandbox](2026-05-25-presents-draft-national-ai-strategy-itu-techafricanews).
developments:
The establishment agreement was signed at Shanghai in July 2026, with the country one of twenty-nine signatory states and one of ten African ones; no ratification step, entry-into-force date or contribution is stated ([membership](2026-07-27-clubofmozambique-waico-founding-member)).

The country is named among African states already implementing an international artificial-intelligence sandbox initiative, with no start date, scope, participant or output held ([sandbox](2026-05-25-presents-draft-national-ai-strategy-itu-techafricanews)).

No domestic model, dataset, compute facility or research output is recorded, so the country's artificial-intelligence position is entirely institutional.

progress: Regressed, the state moving out of both the incumbent operator and a major fixed operator in the same year
summary: A [technical team was formed to sell part of the state stake](2026-08-12-mozambique-tmcel-state-stake-sale-negotiation) in the loss-making incumbent, and a private group [notified a purchase taking it to exclusive control](2026-07-16-visabeira-tvcabo-moz) of a fixed operator.
developments:
The government formed a technical team in August 2026 to negotiate the sale of part of its stake in the incumbent, which carried a US$400m debt in 2023 ([sale](2026-08-12-mozambique-tmcel-state-stake-sale-negotiation)); no buyer, share, valuation, timetable or treatment of the debt is stated ([sale](2026-08-12-mozambique-tmcel-state-stake-sale-negotiation)).

A private group notified the competition authority in July 2026 of the purchase of the incumbent's residual 30 per cent in a fixed operator and its network-engineering arm, taking the group to 80 per cent and exclusive control, with no transaction amount disclosed ([merger](2026-07-16-visabeira-tvcabo-moz)).

Between them these transfer a major fixed operator and its engineering capability out of state part-ownership, and put the incumbent's future ownership in play, with no domestic manufacturing, software or supplier capacity recorded anywhere in the base to set against it.

summary: There is [no national digital literacy programme](2026-08-20-clubofmozambique-national-digital-literacy-programme-ngo), and a non-governmental organisation publicly demanded one in August 2026.
developments:
The absence is dated rather than settled by the source: an organisation used a dialogue-series launch in Maputo on 20 August 2026 to demand a national digital-literacy programme for young people, arguing digital skills are now a precondition for meaningful democratic participation ([demand](2026-08-20-clubofmozambique-national-digital-literacy-programme-ngo)).

A civil-society demand is evidence that no programme exists rather than a programme. No literacy measurement, curriculum or target for the general population is held.

summary: [2,032 professionals were trained](2026-07-23-mozambique-intic-cybersecurity-seminar-laws-13-14-2026-csirt) across public bodies, private firms and the media under the donor project, with fourteen national maturity certifications.
developments:
The cumulative figures are fourteen training actions for thirty institute technicians, 2,032 professionals trained across public bodies, private firms and the media, and fourteen national certifications on an international maturity model ([training](2026-07-23-mozambique-intic-cybersecurity-seminar-laws-13-14-2026-csirt)).

They are the institute's own cumulative figures and the period they cover is not stated, so the base holds a total with no rate behind it and no measure of the civil service population it reached.

summary: A [digital skills programme](2026-08-08-itu-vamoz-digital-project-mozambique) trained fifty young people and five teachers in a pilot, and [EUR 50m was signed](2026-06-19-eeas-mozambique-eu-178m-global-gateway-agreements) for education and skills.
developments:
The programme's reported outputs are a national digital skills assessment informed by more than thirty interviews and a survey of about 400 young people, a pilot that trained fifty young people and five teachers, fifteen women trained under a governance challenge and more than a hundred participants in artificial-intelligence training for young women; no curriculum document, enrolment series or completion rate is published ([outputs](2026-08-08-itu-vamoz-digital-project-mozambique)).

The project behind them runs to 2027 on CHF 2,244,820 with US$8,305,800 of co-financing ([project](2023-01-01-itu-moz-vamoz-digital-2023-laying-the-foundation-for-vamoz-digital), [page](2026-08-08-itu-vamoz-digital-project-mozambique)).

A further EUR 50m was signed in June 2026 to prepare students for a digital and sustainable future, with no recipient organisation, work plan or disbursement named ([agreement](2026-06-19-eeas-mozambique-eu-178m-global-gateway-agreements)).

summary: The [research and education network](2025-10-30-morenet-international-bandwidth-5-to-60-gbps-amlight-sacs) went from 5 to 60 Gbps of international bandwidth, and a [university data centre](2026-08-03-oeconomico-uem-centro-de-dados-banco-mundial) opened in August 2026.
developments:
International bandwidth rose from 5 Gbps on a single route to 60 Gbps over a South Atlantic link with two continental routes in October 2025, restated by the minister as funded for fifteen years; the national backbone that would distribute it to universities was still being expanded at that date ([bandwidth](2025-10-30-morenet-international-bandwidth-5-to-60-gbps-amlight-sacs), [restatement](2026-08-03-lusa-uem-centro-de-dados-morenet-60-gbps-financiada-15-anos)).

The network is operated from the communications ministry's premises, and the minister stated he wants it managed by the universities instead, with no transfer date, instrument or governance model named ([network](2026-08-03-uem-centro-de-dados-transformacao-digital)).

The university data centre opened in August 2026 to carry research, cloud and artificial-intelligence services ([data centre](2026-08-03-oeconomico-uem-centro-de-dados-banco-mundial)).

summary: The minister [proposed transferring the research and education network](2026-08-04-mozambique-govt-universities-cyberattacks-uem-data-centre) from his ministry to the universities, with no date or instrument named.
developments:
The proposal was made at the university data-centre inauguration in August 2026, with no date, instrument or governance model named ([proposal](2026-08-04-mozambique-govt-universities-cyberattacks-uem-data-centre)).

It is the only recorded move to put a national digital asset under academic governance. No research programme, publication or think tank is otherwise recorded contributing to the country's digital policy.

progress: Mixed, EUR 28m signed for women's participation while the gender gap in credit widened
summary: [EUR 28m was signed](2026-06-19-eeas-mozambique-eu-178m-global-gateway-agreements) with a stated focus on women in the digital economy, while the [credit gap widened](2026-07-24-clubofmozambique-atms-pos-lose-ground-mobile-money) from 31-59 to 34-66 per cent.
developments:
The agreement was signed in June 2026 within a four-agreement package of EUR 178m, with the recipient organisation unspecified and no disbursement recorded ([agreement](2026-06-19-eeas-mozambique-eu-178m-global-gateway-agreements)).

Access to credit ran at 31 per cent of women against 59 per cent of men in 2024 and 34 against 66 in 2025, so the gap widened over the same year in which women's mobile money holding rose 24 per cent ([gap](2026-07-24-clubofmozambique-atms-pos-lose-ground-mobile-money)). The account gap narrowed and the credit gap did not, which is the distinction a headline inclusion figure would lose.

progress: Mixed, sixty new rural stations and a subsidy programme against an 80 to 20 urban-rural gap and a major funder's withdrawal
summary: [Sixty rural mobile stations](2025-10-20-60-new-mobile-stations-rural-connectivity-techafricanews) were awarded and [700,000 subsidised smartphones](2026-08-25-diario-economico-mocambique-5g-capitais-provinciais-incm) provided for, against [80 per cent urban penetration and 20 per cent rural](2025-10-20-60-new-mobile-stations-rural-connectivity-techafricanews).
developments:
Sixty mobile stations across nine provinces were awarded in October 2025, each with second and fourth-generation service, a public multimedia centre, solar power, a prepaid public telephone and a hundred handsets; the scope had doubled from thirty sites and no completion date is on record ([award](2025-10-20-60-new-mobile-stations-rural-connectivity-techafricanews), [tender](2025-08-26-rural-connectivity-project-seeks-bids-techafricanews)).

A programme provides for 700,000 subsidised smartphones starting at US$5m and able to grow to US$25m, financed through microcredit and pay-as-you-go models ([smartphones](2026-08-25-diario-economico-mocambique-5g-capitais-provinciais-incm)); no start date, distribution channel or eligibility rule is published ([smartphones](2026-08-25-diario-economico-mocambique-5g-capitais-provinciais-incm)).

The regulator puts penetration at about 80 per cent urban against about 20 per cent rural ([gap](2025-10-20-60-new-mobile-stations-rural-connectivity-techafricanews)), and planned and running inclusion work slowed or stopped after a funder's 2025 wind-down with no replacement named ([withdrawal](2026-08-12-usaid-exit-connectivity-gap-africa)).

summary: An [updated national statistical strategy](2025-12-09-world-bank-data-governance-mozambique-final) is named as in preparation, with no draft, timetable or publication held.
developments:
It is named as one of several strategies in preparation in a December 2025 diagnostic ([diagnostic](2025-12-09-world-bank-data-governance-mozambique-final)).

Nothing else about it is on record: no lead institution beyond the statistics office, no period, no costing and no consultation. It sits alongside a data governance policy, a digital transformation strategy and an artificial-intelligence strategy all in drafting at the same time.
