summary: The [fifth census](2026-08-02-mozambique-invests-430000-in-digital-census-pilot-ahead-of-2027-count) is scheduled for August 2027 as the first run entirely in digital format, on a pilot costing US$430,000 and a US$68m funding shortfall.
developments:
The pilot launched in Magude district in August 2026 at a cost of US$430,000, covering 177 enumeration areas across five administrative posts with 177 enumerators and 38 controllers selected from 260 trained, testing digital cartography, the collection application, the electronic questionnaire, data validation and synchronisation ([pilot](2026-08-02-mozambique-invests-430000-in-digital-census-pilot-ahead-of-2027-count), [training](2026-07-29-jornal-noticias-formacao-censo-piloto-magude)).

The 2027 operation is costed at EUR 96.2m and the institute reported in March 2026 a shortfall of US$68m against the US$110m required, with a funder committing US$12.7m of initial financing ([costing](2026-08-02-governo-testa-piloto-digital-do-censo-populacional-investimento-de-430-mil-dolares)). Which operation pays for the census is unestablished, and no supplier, device count or data-hosting arrangement is reported.

summary: A [microdata catalogue](2026-08-08-mozdata-ine-microdata-catalogue-mozambique) holds 79 statistical operations from four ministries and the statistics office, all under licensed access rather than open download.
developments:
The catalogue held 79 operations at capture in August 2026, depositing from the statistics office, the education ministry, the science ministry and the public works ministry ([catalogue](2026-08-08-mozdata-ine-microdata-catalogue-mozambique)).

Access is licensed, not open, which is the distinction between a microdata archive and an open-data holding. It is the country's only cross-ministry data catalogue.

summary: A [public infrastructure data portal](2026-08-08-ipdp-portal-dados-infraestruturas-publicas-mocambique) publishes road, bridge and project data under an open licence and an international contracting standard.
developments:
The portal is run by the roads fund with foreign development support and was validated as a publisher against the infrastructure contracting standard in 2026 ([portal](2026-08-08-ipdp-portal-dados-infraestruturas-publicas-mocambique)).

It is the only government open-data publication in the base carrying an explicit reuse licence, and it covers one sector. No national open data portal, policy or publication mandate is held.

Where electoral data is concerned, access rests on a bilateral undertaking rather than publication: the elections commission and a civil-society consortium signed a memorandum in April 2023 giving the consortium a right of access to electoral-process information for the 2023 municipal and 2024 general elections in return for a duty to support the electoral bodies ([memorandum](2023-04-27-boletim-das-eleicoes-62)). What was released under it is not held, and the European Union observation mission separately records that most of the commission's 2024 decisions were not accessible from its own website ([mission](2025-01-01-eu-eom-mozambique-2024-final-report)).

summary: A [national flood-mapping capability](2026-08-18-afdb-korea-ricatla-drone-flood-data-mozambique) of nine sensor-equipped drone systems and thirty certified specialists was left by a donor programme in July 2026.
developments:
The capability comprises nine sensor-equipped drone systems, simulators, unmanned surface vessels and data platforms, with thirty specialists from the meteorology institute, the disaster management institute, the remote-sensing centre, the roads administration and the water directorate certified in July 2026 ([programme](2026-08-18-afdb-korea-ricatla-drone-flood-data-mozambique)).

The half-trained cohort was deployed months early into floods in January 2026, which the affected district recorded with no loss of life. The account is the financing bank's own, and no running cost, custodian institution or data-sharing arrangement for the output is stated.

summary: A [bilateral health memorandum](2025-12-15-afghs-mou-mozambique) plans US$1.83bn of support to 2030 including US$83m for health data systems, and [partnership talks](2026-07-06-explores-partnership-with-spacex-techafricanews) were held with a satellite operator.
developments:
The memorandum was signed at Washington in December 2025 for activities running to 2030: planned United States support of US$1,829,380,000 against Mozambique's US$70,573,106, including US$83,072,079 for health data systems ([memorandum](2025-12-15-afghs-mou-mozambique), [record](2025-12-15-state-moz-afghs-data-systems-2025-record)).

The text carries no personal-data, data-ownership, hosting or residency clause, makes failure to fulfil the specimen and data sharing agreements grounds for changing or discontinuing assistance, and lets the United States revisit funding if a mutually acceptable technology roadmap is not finalised ([assessment](2026-01-20 Africa Pushes Back On US Health Deals Over Data, Power)).

A separate government-level meeting with a satellite operator discussed connectivity, digital infrastructure and small-business participation, with no agreement, amount or timetable announced ([talks](2026-07-06-explores-partnership-with-spacex-techafricanews)).

summary: Chinese engagement runs to a [US$132m network facility](2020-01-01-eximbank-cn-moz-002-modernization-and-expansion-of-the-national), [local cloud services](2024-06-10 BCX brings Alibaba Cloud to Mozambique) billed in local currency, and [city surveillance cameras](2026-03-01 Smart City Surveillance in Africa (IDS 2026)) reported concentrated in opposition areas.
developments:
The network modernisation facility was committed in 2020 with no signed loan agreement public ([facility](2020-01-01-eximbank-cn-moz-002-modernization-and-expansion-of-the-national)).

Local cloud services launched in Maputo billed in local currency in 2024, and nothing on the deployment has entered the base since ([cloud](2024-06-10 BCX brings Alibaba Cloud to Mozambique)).

A research report of March 2026 records cameras from three Chinese suppliers concentrated in political-opposition areas in the absence of adequate legal regulation or oversight; it is researcher-reported, and no contract, financier, deployment date, supplier split or camera count for the country is held ([surveillance](2026-03-01 Smart City Surveillance in Africa (IDS 2026))).

summary: Four agreements worth [EUR 178m](2026-06-19-eeas-mozambique-eu-178m-global-gateway-agreements) were signed in June 2026, of which EUR 28m is digital transformation and [EUR 50m](2026-06-19-eeas-mozambique-eu-178m-global-gateway-agreements) education and skills.
developments:
The package was signed at a business forum on 9 June 2026, with EUR 28m for digital transformation focused on women's participation in the digital economy and the recipient organisation unspecified ([package](2026-06-19-eeas-mozambique-eu-178m-global-gateway-agreements)).

A further EUR 50m covers preparing students for a digital and sustainable future, with no recipient organisation, work plan or disbursement named ([education](2026-06-19-eeas-mozambique-eu-178m-global-gateway-agreements)).

No disbursement against either is recorded, and an earlier European digital programme committed in 2022 has nothing disbursed on the published record.

summary: An [information technology park](2025-04-01-india-mozambique-bilateral-relations-mea-brief) was delivered under an Indian concessional line of credit, with no location, value or completion date stated.
developments:
The park is named in an Indian bilateral brief of April 2025 as delivered under a concessional line of credit; the brief states no location, value or completion date ([brief](2025-04-01-india-mozambique-bilateral-relations-mea-brief)).

It is the only Indian digital engagement on record for the country, and nothing in the base establishes whether the park is operating.

summary: A [new voter register is produced for each election](2025-01-01-eu-eom-mozambique-2024-final-report) rather than maintained continuously, and the observation mission records a notable lack of confidence in its reliability.
developments:
The European Union observation mission on the 9 October 2024 general elections records that a new voter register is produced for each election, which it names as part of what makes elections expensive, and a notable lack of confidence in the register's reliability given discrepancies between it and the statistics institute's population projections ([mission](2025-01-01-eu-eom-mozambique-2024-final-report)).

The election administration published no report on the voter registration process, and the mission recommends updating the register from other reliable existing data sources, naming the civil registry ([mission](2025-01-01-eu-eom-mozambique-2024-final-report)).

No register size, update cycle or duplicate rate is published by the election administration.

summary: A [nine-digit single taxpayer identification number](2025-01-01-nuit-frequently-asked-questions) assigned by the revenue authority is required of natural and legal persons for all income including customs.
developments:
The number is assigned by the revenue authority to natural and legal persons regardless of income level and is required for all income including customs, obtained at a tax office against an identity document, passport, birth certificate, voter registration card or driving licence ([guidance](2025-01-01-nuit-frequently-asked-questions)).

The held record is the revenue authority's own guidance page, retrieved from a web archive after the live site failed to answer. No register size, issuance figure or linkage to the national identity system is published.

summary: A [national postal address code](2020-07-23-new-postal-address-code-mozambique) was piloted at one district in 2020 against a five-year, US$33 million rollout, and nothing on it since is held.
developments:
The regulator inaugurated a pilot covering 1,500 homes and other premises and more than 1,200 streets at Manhica in July 2020, with Chimoio in preparation and Matola, Beira, Quelimane, Nampula and Nacala to follow over five years ([pilot](2020-07-23-new-postal-address-code-mozambique)).

The regulator's feasibility study puts the cost of implementing the code at at least US$33 million, from state funds and cooperation partners ([study](2020-07-23-new-postal-address-code-mozambique)).

The base holds nothing on the code after July 2020, so the five-year rollout would have run its course unobserved.

summary: An [education management information system](2024-06-25-milange-district-emis-scaling-school-level) is being pushed from district to school level in one district of more than 300 schools, with no national statement held.
developments:
Milange district in Zambezia, with more than 300 schools, has scaled use of the education management information system down from the district to the individual school so that schools analyse their own data, under a Global Partnership for Education project ([district](2024-06-25-milange-district-emis-scaling-school-level)).

Regional policy work on responsive education-data policies runs alongside it ([policy](2025-01-01-building-responsive-emis-policies-robust-education-data)).

The national system's coverage, data quality and publication arrangements are not held: the base carries one district's initiative and a regional policy discussion, not a national statement.

summary: An [integrated agricultural platform](2025-12-18-ministry-agriculture-integrated-digital-ecosystem) in preparation would carry producer registration and production plot mapping alongside the existing [land-use right system](2019-07-19-fnds-sigit-lims-review-final-report).
developments:
The agriculture, environment and fisheries ministry is preparing a single portal to consolidate services across the agricultural value chain, to carry digital producer registration, production plot mapping, national production certification and seed and input quality control, and to establish export traceability from input to final consumer, with digital land mapping and registration stated to be under way alongside it ([platform](2025-12-18-ministry-agriculture-integrated-digital-ecosystem)).

It was announced by a national director at a private-sector forum, and no budget, supplier, timetable or data-protection arrangement is stated for a system that would register producers and map their plots.

The existing land-use right system digitises application processing, with 563,765 requests recorded, 77 per cent processed and 68 per cent delivered to beneficiaries ([system](2019-07-19-fnds-sigit-lims-review-final-report)); that figure is from 2019 and nothing later is held.

summary: [Birth notifications](2025-01-01-jembi-mozambique-case-study) pass from hospitals into the civil register in real time, and [laboratory results](2025-10-29-connecting-health-information-systems-hiv-care) now reach clinicians without printing or re-keying.
developments:
Electronic birth notifications pass in real time from the hospital birth module into the electronic civil registration system over an interoperability layer, launched on 22 July 2024 after an April-May 2024 pilot in Inhambane province, where the facilities using the birth module grew from five to nineteen and over 11,589 newborns were registered digitally ([integration](2025-01-01-jembi-mozambique-case-study), [launch](2024-08-14-jembi-birth-registration-interoperability)).

Viral load results generated in the laboratory information system now reach clinicians through the electronic patient tracking system without printing or one-by-one re-keying, which was the previous route ([results](2025-10-29-connecting-health-information-systems-hiv-care)).

Both are reported by implementing partners. Nationwide expansion of birth notification is stated as a plan with no date, no figure later than 2024 is held for it, and no coverage, turnaround-time or error-rate figure is published for the laboratory link.

summary: [Hospital births notify the civil register electronically](2025-01-01-jembi-mozambique-case-study) in nineteen facilities of one province, against a civil registration system the Code integrates with the identity system.
developments:
Real-time digital birth registration launched on 22 July 2024, connecting the hospital birth module to the electronic civil registration system; the pilot expanded from five to nineteen health facilities in Inhambane province and registered over 11,589 newborns, with health workers entering birth data directly and receiving instant confirmation ([integration](2025-01-01-jembi-mozambique-case-study)).

The civil registration system is itself established by the revised Civil Registration Code as integrated with the national identity and health systems ([code](2024-01-01-mozambique-crvs-law-policy-summary)).

Coverage is one province of eleven, nationwide expansion carries no date, and no figure later than 2024 is held.
